briefdescription.para: SM_Partition(Default) - Try to create the complement interval so it doesn't overlap any other intervals, and the original interval is partitioned.

detaileddescription.para: This may require a large number of back copies and extra PHI-defs. Only segments marked with overlapIntv will be overlapping.

briefdescription.para: SM_Size - Overlap intervals to minimize the number of inserted COPY instructions.

detaileddescription.para: Copies to the complement interval are hoisted to their common dominator, so only one COPY is required per value in the complement interval. This also means that no extra PHI-defs need to be inserted in the complement interval.

briefdescription.para: SM_Speed - Overlap intervals to minimize the expected execution frequency of the inserted copies.

detaileddescription.para: This is very similar to SM_Size, but the complement interval may get some extra PHI-defs.

briefdescription.para: ComplementSpillMode - Select how the complement live range should be created.

detaileddescription.para: SplitEditor automatically creates interval 0 to contain anything that isn't added to another interval. This complement interval can get quite complicated, and it can sometimes be an advantage to allow it to overlap the other intervals. If it is going to spill anyway, no registers are wasted by keeping a value in two places at the same time.

briefdescription.para: Edit - The current parent register and new intervals created.
Index into Edit of the currently open interval.

detaileddescription.para: The index 0 is used for the complement, so the first interval started by openIntv will be 1.

briefdescription.para: The current spill mode, selected by reset().
Allocator for the interval map.

detaileddescription.para: This will eventually be shared with SlotIndexes and LiveIntervals.

briefdescription.para: RegAssign - Map of the assigned register indexes.

detaileddescription.para: Edit.get(RegAssign.lookup(Idx)) is the register that should be live at Idx.

briefdescription.para: Values - keep track of the mapping from parent values to values in the new intervals.

detaileddescription.para: Given a pair (RegIdx, ParentVNI->id), Values contains:

listitem.para: No entry - the value is not mapped to Edit.get(RegIdx).

(Null, false) - the value is mapped to multiple values in Edit.get(RegIdx). Each value is represented by a minimal live range at its def. The full live range can be inferred exactly from the range of RegIdx in RegAssign.
(Null, true). As above, but the ranges in RegAssign are too large, and the live range must be recomputed using ::extend().
(VNI, false) The value is mapped to a single new value. The new value has no live ranges anywhere.

briefdescription.para: LICalc - Cache for computing live ranges and SSA update.

detaileddescription.para: Each instance can only handle non-overlapping live ranges, so use a separate LiveIntervalCalc instance for the complement interval when in spill mode.

briefdescription.para: getLICalc - Return the LICalc to use for RegIdx.

detaileddescription.para: In spill mode, the complement interval can overlap the other intervals, so it gets its own LICalc instance. When not in spill mode, all intervals can share one.

briefdescription.para: Add a segment to the interval LI for the value number VNI.

detaileddescription.para: If LI has subranges, corresponding segments will be added to them as well, but with newly created value numbers. If Original is true, dead def will only be added a subrange of LI if the corresponding subrange of the original interval has a def at this index. Otherwise, all subranges of LI will be updated.

memberdef.name: defValue

briefdescription.para: defValue - define a value in RegIdx from ParentVNI at Idx.

detaileddescription.para: Idx does not have to be ParentVNI->def, but it must be contained within ParentVNI's live range in ParentLI. The new value is added to the value map. The value being defined may either come from rematerialization (or an inserted copy), or it may be coming from the original interval. The parameter Original should be true in the latter case, otherwise it should be false. Return the new LI value.

briefdescription.para: forceRecompute - Force the live range of ParentVNI in RegIdx to be recomputed by LiveRangeCalc::extend regardless of the number of defs.

detaileddescription.para: This is used for values whose live range doesn't match RegAssign exactly. They could have rematerialized, or back-copies may have been moved.

briefdescription.para: Calls forceRecompute() on any affected regidx and on ParentVNI predecessors in case of a phi definition.

detaileddescription.para: Return the new value.

briefdescription.para: removeBackCopies - Remove the copy instructions that defines the values in the vector in the complement interval.
getShallowDominator - Returns the least busy dominator of MBB that is also dominated by DefMBB.

detaileddescription.para: Busy is measured by loop depth.

briefdescription.para: Find out all the backCopies dominated by others.
Hoist back-copies to the complement interval.

detaileddescription.para: For SM_Size mode, find a common dominator for all the back-copies for the same ParentVNI and hoist the backcopies to the dominator BB.
It tries to hoist all the back-copies to one BB if it is beneficial, or else simply remove redundant backcopies dominated by others.
For SM_Speed mode, if the common dominator is hot and it is not beneficial to do the hoisting, simply remove the dominated backcopies for the same ParentVNI.

Return true if any ranges were skipped.
Values that were rematerialized are left alone, they need LICalc.extend().

briefdescription.para: Create a new SplitEditor for editing the LiveInterval analyzed by SA.

detaileddescription.para: Newly created intervals will be appended to newIntervals.

briefdescription.para: reset - Prepare for a new split.
Create a new virtual register and live interval.

detaileddescription.para: Return the interval index, starting from 1. Interval index 0 is the implicit complement interval.

briefdescription.para: currentIntv - Return the current interval index.
selectIntv - Select a previously opened interval index.
enterIntvBefore - Enter the open interval before the instruction at Idx.

detaileddescription.para: If the parent interval is not live before Idx, a COPY is not inserted. Return the beginning of the new live range.

briefdescription.para: enterIntvAfter - Enter the open interval after the instruction at Idx.

detaileddescription.para: Return the beginning of the new live range.

briefdescription.para: enterIntvAtEnd - Enter the open interval at the end of MBB.

detaileddescription.para: Use the open interval from the inserted copy to the MBB end. Return the beginning of the new live range.

briefdescription.para: useIntv - indicate that all instructions in MBB should use OpenLI.
useIntv - indicate that all instructions in range should use OpenLI.
leaveIntvAfter - Leave the open interval after the instruction at Idx.

detaileddescription.para: Return the end of the live range.

briefdescription.para: leaveIntvBefore - Leave the open interval before the instruction at Idx.

detaileddescription.para: Return the end of the live range.

briefdescription.para: leaveIntvAtTop - Leave the interval at the top of MBB.

detaileddescription.para: Add liveness from the MBB top to the copy. Return the end of the live range.

briefdescription.para: overlapIntv - Indicate that all instructions in range should use the open interval if End does not have tied-def usage of the register and in this case complement interval is used.

detaileddescription.para: Let the complement interval be live.
This doubles the register pressure, but is sometimes required to deal with register uses after the last valid split point.
The Start index should be a return value from a leaveIntv* call, and End should be in the same basic block. The parent interval must have the same value across the range.

briefdescription.para: finish - after all the new live ranges have been created, compute the remaining live range, and rewrite instructions to use the new registers.

parameterdescription.para: When not null, this vector will map each live range in Edit back to the indices returned by openIntv. There may be extra indices created by dead code elimination.

briefdescription.para: dump - print the current interval mapping to dbgs().
splitSingleBlock - Split CurLI into a separate live interval around the uses in a single block.

detaileddescription.para: This is intended to be used as part of a larger split, and doesn't call finish().

memberdef.name: splitLiveThroughBlock

briefdescription.para: splitLiveThroughBlock - Split CurLI in the given block such that it enters the block in IntvIn and leaves it in IntvOut.

detaileddescription.para: There may be uses in the block, but they will be ignored when placing split points.

parameterdescription.para: When set, leave IntvIn before this point.
When set, enter IntvOut after this point.

briefdescription.para: splitRegInBlock - Split CurLI in the given block such that it enters the block in IntvIn and leaves it on the stack (or not at all).

detaileddescription.para: Split points are placed in a way that avoids putting uses in the stack interval. This may require creating a local interval when there is interference.

parameterdescription.para: Interval index entering the block. Not 0.
When set, leave IntvIn before this point.

briefdescription.para: splitRegOutBlock - Split CurLI in the given block such that it enters the block on the stack (or isn't live-in at all) and leaves it in IntvOut.

detaileddescription.para: Split points are placed to avoid interference and such that the uses are not in the stack interval. This may require creating a local interval when there is interference.

parameterdescription.para: When set, enter IntvOut after this point.

briefdescription.para: SplitEditor - Edit machine code and LiveIntervals for live range splitting.

listitem.para: Create a SplitEditor from a SplitAnalysis.
Start a new live interval with openIntv.
Mark the places where the new interval is entered using enterIntv*
Mark the ranges where the new interval is used with useIntv*
Mark the places where the interval is exited with exitIntv*.
Finish the current interval with closeIntv and repeat from 2.
